about: Sourced life stories for people around David and his house: his family, his captains, his priests and prophet, and two later figures named with them. Written from the KJV text itself; there is no reviewed dossier for these people.

joab-1sa-26-6.short: A son of Zeruiah and captain of David's host, who killed Abner and Amasa, struck Absalom with darts, and was put to death after fleeing to the altar.

paragraphs.text: Joab was a son of Zeruiah, with his brothers Abishai and Asahel; Chronicles lists Zeruiah as a sister of David and his brothers. Scripture never names his father, but Asahel was buried "in the sepulchre of his father, which was in Beth-lehem." At the pool of Gibeon Joab led David's servants against Abner and the servants of Ish-bosheth. There Abner killed Asahel, and when Abner called out, "Shall the sword devour for ever?", Joab blew a trumpet and the pursuit stopped.

When Abner came to David at Hebron and was sent away in peace, Joab told the king, "Thou knowest Abner the son of Ner, that he came to deceive thee". Without David's knowledge he brought Abner back, took him aside in the gate and killed him, "for the blood of Asahel his brother"; Samuel says Joab and Abishai his brother slew Abner. David declared himself guiltless, let the blood rest on Joab and his father's house, and said, "these men the sons of Zeruiah be too hard for me".

Chronicles adds that when David went against the Jebusites at Jerusalem, Joab "went first up, and was chief", and that he repaired the rest of the city. He was over the host. He led the army against Ammon and the Syrians, telling Abishai, "Be of good courage, and let us play the men for our people", and he besieged Rabbah. Kings later recalls that he stayed six months in Edom "until he had cut off every male in Edom".

During the siege of Rabbah, David sent a letter to Joab by the hand of Uriah the Hittite, and Joab set Uriah "unto a place where he knew that valiant men were"; Uriah died, and Joab sent word to David. When the city was nearly taken, Joab sent for David to take it, "lest I take the city, and it be called after my name." Later Joab "perceived that the king's heart was toward Absalom", sent a wise woman of Tekoah to the king with words he put in her mouth, and brought Absalom home from Geshur.

When Absalom rose against his father, David told his captains, "Deal gently for my sake with the young man". A man saw Absalom hanging in an oak and would not touch him, but Joab "took three darts in his hand, and thrust them through the heart of Absalom", and his armourbearers slew him. When David mourned, Joab told him he had shamed his servants, and the king went and sat in the gate. David then promised Joab's place to Amasa; Joab took Amasa by the beard "to kiss him" and killed him with his sword, then besieged Sheba the son of Bichri at Abel until the city threw Sheba's head over the wall to him.

When David ordered Israel numbered, Joab asked, "why doth my lord the king delight in this thing?", but the king's word prevailed and Joab brought him the count. Chronicles adds that he did not count Levi and Benjamin, "for the king's word was abominable to Joab". In David's old age Joab followed Adonijah, and David charged Solomon not to let "his hoar head go down to the grave in peace." When the news reached him, Joab fled to the tabernacle and caught hold of the horns of the altar; told to come out, he said, "Nay; but I will die here." Benaiah the son of Jehoiada killed him, and he was buried "in his own house in the wilderness."

abner-1sa-14-50.short: The son of Ner and captain of Saul's host, who made Ish-bosheth king, then turned to David, and was killed by Joab in the gate of Hebron.

paragraphs.text: Samuel's book names the captain of Saul's host as "Abner, the son of Ner, Saul's uncle", and adds that "Ner the father of Abner was the son of Abiel". Saul's father Kish is also called the son of Abiel. Chronicles, listing Saul's family, says instead, "Ner begat Kish, and Kish begat Saul".

Abner stood at Saul's side. When David went out against Goliath, Saul asked him whose son the youth was, and he answered, "I cannot tell"; afterwards he brought David before Saul with the Philistine's head in his hand. He sat by Saul at the feast of the new moon when David's place was empty. When David came into Saul's camp by night and took the spear and the cruse of water, he called out to Abner, "Art not thou a valiant man?", and said Abner had not kept his master.

After Saul's death Abner took Saul's son Ish-bosheth to Mahanaim and made him king over Israel, while Judah followed David. At the pool of Gibeon his men were beaten by David's servants under Joab. Joab's brother Asahel chased him and would not turn aside, and Abner killed him with the hinder end of his spear. At evening Abner called to Joab, "Shall the sword devour for ever?", and the fighting stopped.

As the long war between the houses of Saul and David went on, Abner "made himself strong for the house of Saul". When Ish-bosheth accused him over Saul's concubine Rizpah, Abner was very angry and sent to David to make a league and bring all Israel to him. At David's demand Michal was sent back to David, and Abner spoke with the elders of Israel and with Benjamin, then came to Hebron with twenty men, where David made them a feast and sent Abner away in peace.

Joab, coming back from a raid, sent after Abner and brought him back from the well of Sirah without David's knowledge, and killed him in the gate "for the blood of Asahel his brother." David followed the bier, wept at Abner's grave in Hebron, and lamented, "Died Abner as a fool dieth?" He told his servants, "there is a prince and a great man fallen this day in Israel", and all Israel understood that the king had no part in the killing. Later the head of Ish-bosheth was buried in Abner's sepulchre in Hebron.

Solomon later spoke of Abner and Amasa as "two men more righteous and better than he" whom Joab had killed. Chronicles lists things "Abner the son of Ner" had dedicated, and in its list of rulers over the tribes gives Benjamin's as "Jaasiel the son of Abner", without saying which Abner.

absalom-2sa-3-3.short: David's third son, born at Hebron to Maacah of Geshur, who had his brother Amnon killed, rose against his father, and was slain in the wood of Ephraim.

paragraphs.text: Absalom was David's third son, born at Hebron; his mother was Maacah, the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur. "In all Israel there was none to be so much praised as Absalom for his beauty", and he cut his heavy hair once a year and weighed it at two hundred shekels. Three sons and a daughter, Tamar, were born to him. In his lifetime he also set up a pillar in the king's dale, saying, "I have no son to keep my name in remembrance", and called it after his own name.

When his brother Amnon forced his sister Tamar, Absalom took her into his house and spoke to Amnon "neither good nor bad". Two years later he invited all the king's sons to his sheepshearing at Baal-hazor and had his servants kill Amnon when he was merry with wine. Then he fled to Talmai king of Geshur and stayed there three years, and David mourned for his son every day.

Joab brought him back to Jerusalem, but for two full years he did not see the king's face. When Joab would not come to him, Absalom had his servants set Joab's barley field on fire; then Joab went to the king, Absalom bowed before his father, "and the king kissed Absalom."

Afterwards he got chariots and horses and fifty men to run before him, and stood by the gate telling men who came for judgment that no one was deputed to hear them: "so Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel." He went to Hebron saying he had a vow to pay, sent for David's counsellor Ahithophel, and sent spies through the tribes to say, "Absalom reigneth in Hebron". David fled from Jerusalem. In the city Absalom went in to his father's concubines on the roof "in the sight of all Israel", and he chose the counsel of Hushai over Ahithophel's.

Absalom made Amasa captain of his host, crossed the Jordan, and pitched in the land of Gilead. David told his captains, "Deal gently for my sake with the young man". In the wood of Ephraim Absalom's men were beaten, and as he rode his mule under a great oak his head caught in the oak. Joab thrust three darts through his heart, ten young men who bore Joab's armour slew him, and they cast him into a great pit and laid a very great heap of stones on him. David wept, "O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom!"

The title of Psalm 3 sets it at the time David fled from Absalom his son. Kings names the mother of Abijam and of Asa as "Maachah, the daughter of Abishalom"; Chronicles says Rehoboam took "Maachah the daughter of Absalom", who bore him Abijah. Neither book says that this Absalom was David's son.

jonathan-1sa-13-2.short: Saul's son, a warrior who attacked a Philistine garrison with only his armourbearer, loved David as his own soul, and died with his father on mount Gilboa.

paragraphs.text: Jonathan was a son of Saul; Samuel names him first among Saul's sons, and Chronicles gives the line "Ner begat Kish, and Kish begat Saul, and Saul begat Jonathan". When Saul chose three thousand men, a thousand were with Jonathan in Gibeah, and he struck the Philistine garrison in Geba. On the day of battle only Saul and Jonathan had sword and spear.

Without telling his father, he and his armourbearer climbed to a Philistine garrison between two sharp rocks: "there is no restraint to the LORD to save by many or by few." They killed about twenty men, and "there was trembling in the host". Not having heard his father's oath that no one should eat before evening, he tasted honey from the end of his rod. When the lot fell on him, Saul said he must die, but the people rescued him: "he hath wrought with God this day."

When David had finished speaking with Saul after killing Goliath, "the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David". Jonathan made a covenant with him and gave him his robe, his garments, his sword, his bow and his girdle. When Saul told him and his servants to kill David, Jonathan warned David and spoke well of him to his father, and Saul swore that David would not be slain.

At the feast of the new moon David's place was empty, and when Jonathan asked why David should die, Saul cast a javelin at him. Next morning he shot arrows in the field as the agreed sign, and the two parted: "The LORD be between me and thee, and between my seed and thy seed for ever." Later he went to David in the wood, "strengthened his hand in God", and said, "thou shalt be king over Israel, and I shall be next unto thee".

The Philistines killed Jonathan with his brothers Abinadab and Malchi-shua on mount Gilboa, and the men of Jabesh-gilead took the bodies from the wall of Beth-shan and buried their bones. David lamented: "I am distressed for thee, my brother Jonathan: very pleasant hast thou been unto me: thy love to me was wonderful, passing the love of women." Later David brought the bones of Saul and Jonathan and buried them in the sepulchre of Kish in Zelah of Benjamin.

Jonathan's son Mephibosheth was five years old when the news came; his nurse fled with him, and he fell and became lame. For Jonathan's sake David restored to him all the land of Saul and had him eat at the king's table, and later spared him "because of the LORD's oath that was between them". Chronicles calls Jonathan's son Merib-baal.

jesse-rut-4-17.short: A Beth-lehemite, grandson of Boaz and Ruth, whose youngest son David was anointed by Samuel; Scripture often calls David simply the son of Jesse.

paragraphs.text: Jesse was the son of Obed, whom Ruth bore to Boaz; the book of Ruth ends, "Obed begat Jesse, and Jesse begat David." Samuel calls him "that Ephrathite of Beth-lehem-judah" and says that in Saul's days he was counted an old man. Scripture does not name David's mother.

Samuel's book says Jesse had eight sons, of whom the three eldest, Eliab, Abinadab and Shammah, followed Saul to war. Chronicles names seven, Eliab, Abinadab, Shimma, Nethaneel, Raddai, Ozem and David, and gives them two sisters, Zeruiah and Abigail.

The LORD sent Samuel to Jesse at Beth-lehem: "I have provided me a king among his sons." Jesse made seven of his sons pass before Samuel, and none of them was chosen. The youngest was keeping the sheep; when he was fetched, Samuel anointed him in the midst of his brothers.

When Saul sent for the son who could play, Jesse sent David to him with an ass laden with bread, a bottle of wine and a kid. Later he sent David to the camp with parched corn and ten loaves for his brothers. When Saul asked whose son he was, David answered, "I am the son of thy servant Jesse the Beth-lehemite."

When David fled from Saul, his brothers and all his father's house came to him at the cave of Adullam, and David asked the king of Moab to let his father and mother stay with him "till I know what God will do for me." Jesse himself does not appear again. His name stays with his son: Saul and Nabal speak of David as "the son of Jesse", and David's last words begin, "David the son of Jesse said".
Isaiah speaks of "a rod out of the stem of Jesse" and "a root of Jesse", and Paul quotes the second in Romans. Matthew and Luke both include Jesse in the genealogy of Jesus.

zeruiah-1sa-26-6.short: The mother of Joab, Abishai and Asahel, named almost only through her sons; Chronicles lists her as a sister of David and his brothers.

paragraphs.text: Scripture tells almost nothing of Zeruiah herself. Nearly every verse that names her does so in calling one of her three sons, Joab, Abishai and Asahel, "the son of Zeruiah"; all three fought for David. Her husband is never named, though Asahel was buried "in the sepulchre of his father, which was in Beth-lehem."

Chronicles, listing the children of Jesse, says of his sons: "Whose sisters were Zeruiah, and Abigail. And the sons of Zeruiah; Abishai, and Joab, and Asahel, three." Samuel, introducing Absalom's captain Amasa, calls Amasa's mother "Abigail the daughter of Nahash, sister to Zeruiah Joab's mother."

David spoke of her sons together more than once. After Abner's death he said, "these men the sons of Zeruiah be too hard for me", and when Abishai twice wanted to put Shimei to death, David answered, "What have I to do with you, ye sons of Zeruiah?"

zadok-2sa-8-17.short: The son of Ahitub, priest with Abiathar in David's days, who stayed loyal through Absalom's revolt, anointed Solomon king, and took Abiathar's place.

paragraphs.text: Zadok was the son of Ahitub. Chronicles traces his line from Aaron through Eleazar, and says David divided the priests between "Zadok of the sons of Eleazar, and Ahimelech of the sons of Ithamar". In the list of David's officers Samuel names the priests as "Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar"; in the same list Chronicles has "Abimelech the son of Abiathar".

Chronicles says David called Zadok and Abiathar with the chief of the Levites to bring the ark up to the place he had prepared for it. It says he then left Zadok and his brethren the priests before the tabernacle of the LORD in the high place at Gibeon, to offer burnt offerings morning and evening.

When David fled from Absalom, Zadok and the Levites came out bearing the ark of the covenant, and David told him, "Carry back the ark of God into the city". Zadok and Abiathar stayed in Jerusalem; Hushai passed Absalom's counsel to them, and their sons Ahimaaz and Jonathan carried word to David, once hiding in a well at Bahurim. After the battle Ahimaaz ran to bring David the news, and David sent to Zadok and Abiathar to ask the elders of Judah to bring the king back.

Zadok was not with Adonijah when he tried to take the throne. At David's command Zadok and Nathan the prophet anointed Solomon at Gihon with a horn of oil from the tabernacle, and the people said, "God save king Solomon." Solomon put Zadok in Abiathar's place; Chronicles says Zadok was anointed "to be priest" when Solomon was made king the second time. Kings still lists "Zadok and Abiathar" as priests among Solomon's princes.

His name stayed with the priesthood. Chronicles names "Azariah the chief priest of the house of Zadok" in Hezekiah's days, and Ezekiel's vision of the temple gives the charge of the altar to "the sons of Zadok", who "went not astray when the children of Israel went astray".

abiathar-1sa-22-20.short: The son of Ahimelech who escaped Saul's slaughter of the priests at Nob, served David with the ephod, and was sent home to Anathoth by Solomon.

paragraphs.text: Abiathar was a son of Ahimelech the son of Ahitub, the priest at Nob. When Ahimelech gave the fleeing David hallowed bread and Goliath's sword, Saul had Doeg the Edomite kill the priests, "fourscore and five persons that did wear a linen ephod", and Doeg struck Nob, the city of the priests. One son, Abiathar, escaped and fled to David, who told him, "I have occasioned the death of all the persons of thy father's house", and, "Abide thou with me, fear not".

He came down to David with an ephod in his hand. At Keilah David told him, "Bring hither the ephod", and asked the LORD whether Saul would come; at Ziklag he asked again through Abiathar whether to pursue the Amalekites, and was told, "Pursue".

In David's reign he was priest with Zadok. When David fled from Absalom, Abiathar went up while Zadok and the Levites set down the ark; then the two of them carried it back to Jerusalem at the king's word, stayed there, and sent news through their sons Ahimaaz and Jonathan. Samuel and Chronicles also name a priest "Ahimelech the son of Abiathar" in David's time.

In David's old age Abiathar went with Joab after Adonijah and was at Adonijah's feast; his son Jonathan brought the news that Solomon had been anointed. Solomon sent him to his own fields at Anathoth, "for thou art worthy of death", but would not put him to death at that time, because he had borne the ark before David and been afflicted in all that David suffered. So Solomon thrust Abiathar out from being priest, and Kings says this fulfilled the word of the LORD "concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh". It still lists "Zadok and Abiathar" as priests among Solomon's princes.

In Mark, Jesus says that David went into the house of God "in the days of Abiathar the high priest" and ate the shewbread. In 1 Samuel the priest at Nob who gave David the hallowed bread is Ahimelech, Abiathar's father.

nathan-2sa-7-2.short: The prophet in David's court who brought God's promise of a lasting house, rebuked David over Bath-sheba, and helped bring Solomon to the throne.

paragraphs.text: Scripture gives Nathan no father, tribe or home; it calls him "Nathan the prophet". He first appears when David, living in a house of cedar, wanted to build a house for the ark. Nathan told him, "Go, do all that is in thine heart", but that night the word of the LORD came to him: David's son would build the house, and the LORD would make David a house and establish his throne for ever. Chronicles tells the same message in slightly different words.

After David took Bath-sheba and had Uriah killed, "the LORD sent Nathan unto David". Nathan told of a rich man who took a poor man's one little ewe lamb, and when David said the man should die, Nathan answered, "Thou art the man." He said the sword would never depart from David's house and that the child would die; when David said, "I have sinned against the LORD", Nathan answered, "The LORD also hath put away thy sin; thou shalt not die." The title of Psalm 51 sets it at the time Nathan came to David.

When Solomon was born, the name Jedidiah was given him through Nathan. Later, when Adonijah made himself king while David was old, Nathan, who had not been invited, told Bath-sheba to go to the king and remind him of his oath, and came in himself to confirm her words. At David's command he and Zadok the priest anointed Solomon at Gihon.

Chronicles says the acts of David and of Solomon were written in "the book of Nathan the prophet", and that the Levites' music in the temple followed "the commandment of David, and of Gad the king's seer, and Nathan the prophet". Scripture does not tell of his death. David also had a son named Nathan, and two of Solomon's officers, Azariah and Zabud, are each called "the son of Nathan"; Kings does not say which Nathan.

asaph-1ch-6-39.short: A Levite singer, the son of Berachiah, whom David set over the music before the ark; the titles of twelve psalms bear his name.

paragraphs.text: Asaph was a Levite, "the son of Berachiah", whose line Chronicles traces back to Gershom the son of Levi. Among the singers David set over the service of song, he is called the brother of Heman, "who stood on his right hand".

When the ark was brought up to Jerusalem, the Levites appointed Heman, Asaph and Ethan as singers "to sound with cymbals of brass". Before the ark Asaph was "the chief" and made a sound with cymbals, and on that day David first delivered a psalm of thanks "into the hand of Asaph and his brethren". David left Asaph and his brethren to minister before the ark continually, "as every day's work required".

David and the captains of the host set apart his sons Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah and Asarelah, with the sons of Heman and Jeduthun, to "prophesy with harps, with psalteries, and with cymbals", under the hands of their father. When lots were cast for the courses, the first fell to Joseph of the sons of Asaph.

The titles of twelve psalms, Psalm 50 and Psalms 73 to 83, name Asaph; the titles say nothing more about him. In Hezekiah's days the Levites sang praise "with the words of David, and of Asaph the seer".

His name stayed with the singers after him. When Solomon brought the ark into the house of the LORD, Chronicles places there the Levite singers, "all of them of Asaph, of Heman, of Jeduthun", and names later Levites "of the sons of Asaph". Among those who came back from captivity, Ezra counts "the children of Asaph" as a hundred twenty and eight, and Nehemiah as a hundred forty and eight. Nehemiah recalls that "in the days of David and Asaph of old there were chief of the singers".

nebat-1ki-11-26.short: The father of Jeroboam, first king of the northern tribes; Scripture names him only in the phrase Jeroboam the son of Nebat.

paragraphs.text: Scripture tells nothing of Nebat himself. Every verse that names him does so in the phrase "Jeroboam the son of Nebat". When Jeroboam is introduced he is "an Ephrathite of Zereda, Solomon's servant, whose mother's name was Zeruah, a widow woman". Jeroboam's own page tells his story.

The phrase became the way Kings names the first king of the northern tribes, above all in its verdict on later kings of Israel, who "departed not from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin". Chronicles uses it too, in the visions of Iddo the seer "against Jeroboam the son of Nebat".

jehoiada-2ki-11-4.short: The priest who hid the boy Joash in the temple, made him king, had Athaliah put to death, and guided the king while he lived.

paragraphs.text: Scripture does not name Jehoiada's father. When Athaliah destroyed the royal seed, Jehosheba, the daughter of king Joram, hid Ahaziah's son Joash, and he was kept hidden six years in the house of the LORD. Chronicles adds that she (it spells her Jehoshabeath) was "the wife of Jehoiada the priest".

In the seventh year Jehoiada brought the rulers over hundreds, the captains and the guard into the house of the LORD, made a covenant with them, and showed them the king's son. He gave the captains king David's spears and shields from the temple, brought out the boy, put the crown on him and gave him the testimony; they anointed him and said, "God save the king." Chronicles tells it with the Levites gathered out of the cities of Judah, and says "Jehoiada and his sons anointed him".

When Athaliah came in crying, "Treason, Treason", Jehoiada had her taken out of the ranges, saying, "Let her not be slain in the house of the LORD", and she was killed by the king's house. He made a covenant between the LORD, the king and the people, "that they should be the LORD's people"; the people broke down the house of Baal and killed Mattan its priest, and Jehoiada set officers over the house of the LORD and brought the king to his throne. Chronicles adds that he appointed the priests and Levites to their offices "as it was ordained by David", and set porters at the gates.

Joash was seven years old when he began to reign. Kings says he did right "all his days wherein Jehoiada the priest instructed him"; Chronicles says "all the days of Jehoiada the priest", and adds that Jehoiada took two wives for the king. When the priests had not repaired the temple by the king's twenty-third year, Kings says Jehoiada took a chest, bored a hole in its lid and set it beside the altar. Chronicles says the chest was made at the king's commandment and set "without at the gate of the house of the LORD".

Chronicles alone tells of his end. Jehoiada "was full of days when he died", a hundred and thirty years old, and was buried in the city of David among the kings, "because he had done good in Israel, both toward God, and toward his house." After his death the princes of Judah came to the king, he hearkened to them, and they served groves and idols; and when Jehoiada's son Zechariah spoke against it, he was stoned at the king's commandment. Chronicles says Joash "remembered not the kindness which Jehoiada his father had done to him".
